originalTitle: Zambia courts sealed off as election petition deadline looms
title: Big News from Zambia! Our Special Leader is Getting Ready!
content:
Hello, My Amazing Little Explorers!

Hello everyone, it's me, your friendly kid news reporter for Africa! I have some super exciting news to share with you today from a wonderful country called Zambia. Do you know where Zambia is? It’s a beautiful place right here in our amazing continent of Africa, full of kind people and incredible sights! Today, we're talking about something very important happening in Zambia. It's all about how a country chooses its leader and gets ready for them to start their big job. It’s like when you get ready for your first day of school, but much, much bigger!

Meet the President of Zambia!

Every country needs a special person to lead everyone, right? This person helps make big decisions for all the people who live there. In Zambia, just like in many other countries, this special leader is called a President. The President is like the head teacher of the whole country! They work very hard to make sure schools are good, roads are safe, and everyone has what they need to live happy and healthy lives. It’s a very big and important job!

Who is President Hakainde Hichilema?

Guess what? The current President of Zambia is a very nice man named Hakainde Hichilema (that's Ha-kai-nde Hi-chi-le-ma!). He was chosen by the people of Zambia to be their leader. Isn’t that cool? The people themselves picked who they wanted to lead them. President Hichilema is now getting ready for a very, very special moment. It's a bit like getting ready for a big birthday party, but it's for the whole country! He's preparing to officially start his next big term as President.

What is an Election?

So, how do people choose their President? They have something called an election! An election is a really cool way for everyone, when they are grown up, to have a say in who leads their country. It’s a very fair way to choose! During an election, people go to special places to put their choice on a paper. This is called voting! Every single vote is important and helps decide who will be the leader. It’s like a big team deciding who will be their captain. Did you know? When grown-ups vote, they are helping to build the future of their country! It’s a very powerful and important thing to do.

What is an Inauguration?

After people vote and everyone knows who the new President will be, there’s a super big celebration! This celebration is called an inauguration (say: in-aw-gyu-RAY-shun). Can you say that big word? An inauguration is like a giant, happy party where the President officially starts their important job. There are speeches, music, and lots of cheering! Everyone celebrates their new leader and gets excited for the future of their country. President Hichilema is getting ready for his inauguration now!

Sometimes There Are Questions

Sometimes, after a big election, someone might have a question about how everything went. Maybe they think something wasn't quite right or fair. When someone has a question like this, they can make something called a "petition" (say: pe-TISH-un). A petition is like asking a very special grown-up to check everything again, very carefully. They just want to make super-duper sure that the election was fair for everyone. It’s a way to ensure that all the rules were followed. Did you know? Having a way to ask questions helps make sure everything in a country is fair and honest!

Who Checks the Questions?

So, who are these special grown-ups who check the questions? They are called judges! Judges are very smart people who know all the rules and laws of the country. They listen very carefully to everyone. Judges work in special buildings called "courts" (say: korts). You can think of courts as very important classrooms where judges listen to problems and make sure everyone follows the rules fairly. They help solve big problems and make sure justice is done. Did you know? In many countries, judges wear special robes, like fancy uniforms, to show how important their job is!

The Courts Were Closed!

Now, here’s the interesting part of our news story! Recently, the courts in Zambia were closed for a short time for a very special reason. This wasn’t because of a holiday or anything scary, but because of a very important rule! It’s like when your teacher says, "You need to hand in your drawing by playtime!" After playtime, you can't hand in your drawing anymore, right? That special time limit is called a "deadline" (say: DED-line). And it's super important to follow deadlines.

Why Was There a Deadline?

There was a deadline for people to ask their questions, or make their petitions, about the election. This deadline is very important. Once it passes, it means that all the questions have been asked and checked, and the election results are final. This helps the whole country move forward! It means that President Hichilema can now fully get ready for his inauguration without anyone asking new questions about the election. It makes everything clear and ready for the next step. Did you know? Having clear rules and deadlines helps a country stay organized and strong! It's part of what we call "democracy," which means people choose their leaders.

What Happens Now?

So, what happens next? Now that the deadline has passed and all the questions have been checked, everything is clear for President Hichilema. He can now officially prepare for his inauguration! This is wonderful news for everyone in Zambia. He will take a special promise, called an oath, to work very hard and do his best for all the people in Zambia. It's a very serious and exciting moment. It shows he is ready to take on the big responsibility of leading his country.

Why Is This News Important?

This news is super important for all the children in Zambia, and all of us watching from Africa and around the world! It means their country has a clear and chosen leader who is ready to get to work. A clear leader helps make sure everything runs smoothly in the country. This means the President can focus on important things like building more schools, making sure there are good hospitals, and creating safe and fun places for children to play. It means a bright and hopeful future for everyone in Zambia! Did you know? Zambia is famous for the incredible Victoria Falls, one of the biggest waterfalls in the world! It also has amazing wildlife like elephants and giraffes.

A Bright Future for Zambia!

So, there you have it, my little friends! Zambia is moving forward with its chosen leader, President Hichilema. He is ready to serve his country and help make it an even better place. We wish him good luck and send big cheers from all of us! It’s an exciting time for Zambia, a fantastic country in our amazing continent of Africa. Keep being curious and keep learning about our wonderful world! Bye for now!
summary: President Hakainde Hichilema of Zambia is getting ready for his second inauguration after the deadline for election questions passed, making way for a clear path forward for the country.
whyMatters: This is important because it means Zambia has a clear leader who can now officially start his big job, which helps the country focus on important things like building schools and keeping everyone safe and happy.

originalTitle: '101-year-old great-grandmother' arrested for selling cannabis in Nigeria
title: A Very Old Great-Grandma and a Story of Rules!
content:
Hello, My Little Friends!

Hello, hello, my wonderful friends! Your kid-friendly news reporter is here from beautiful Africa! I have a very interesting story for you today. It's about rules, safety, and a very, very old lady. Let's listen carefully! This story comes from a country called Nigeria. Nigeria is a big, lovely country in Africa, just like where you are! It has many people and lots of sunshine.

Meet Esther, the Great-Grandma

Our story is about a lady named Esther Ogunmabo. Can you say Esther Ogunmabo? Good job! Esther is very, very special. Do you know why? Because she is 101 years old! Wow! Can you imagine being 101? That's older than your grandma, and probably older than your great-grandma too! Esther is a great-grandmother. That means she has children, and her children have children, and *their* children have children! She has a big family. Did you know? Being a great-grandmother means you have lived for a very, very long time and have seen many, many things happen in the world!

What Happened?

Now, here is the tricky part of the story. Something happened that made people sad. Esther, our 101-year-old great-grandmother, was arrested. "Arrested" means that the people who keep us safe, like the police, took her because she did something against the rules. They took her to ask her questions about what happened. They said she was selling something. Imagine selling sweets or toys. But Esther was selling something called "cannabis." Sometimes people call it "skunk" too. It's a plant, but it's not a plant like the vegetables we eat or the flowers we smell. It's a special kind of plant that is not good for people.

What is "Cannabis" or "Skunk"?

Let's talk about this plant, cannabis. It's a kind of plant that some people use. But it's not like the good plants we use for food or pretty gardens. Cannabis is a drug. What is a drug? Well, some drugs are good medicine that doctors give us when we are sick to make us feel better. Those are good drugs, and we take them only when a doctor says so. But there are other kinds of drugs that are not medicine. These drugs can make people feel strange, or even sick. And they are not good for our bodies or our brains. Cannabis is one of these kinds of plants. Did you know? Not all plants are safe to eat or use. Some plants can make you very, very sick! That's why we should never eat or touch plants we don't know, unless a grown-up tells us it's safe. This cannabis plant is against the law to sell. It is against the law to use. It is against the law to have. Why? Because it can harm people. It can make them unwell. Esther was selling it in small packets, like little sachets. This is not allowed.

Why Are Rules Important?

Why do we have rules? Think about it. We have rules at school, right? Rules like "don't run in the hallway" or "be kind to your friends." These rules help keep everyone safe and happy. It's the same in big countries like Nigeria. There are rules for everyone. These rules are called "laws." Laws help everyone stay safe and make sure things are fair. One of these big rules is about drugs. The law says that plants like cannabis are not allowed. They are illegal. This means you cannot grow them, you cannot sell them, and you cannot use them. Why is this rule so important? Because these things can hurt people. They can make people unwell in their minds and bodies. Grown-ups make these rules to protect everyone, especially children. Did you know? Rules help us live together happily and safely. Imagine if there were no rules for cars on the road! It would be very messy and dangerous!

Who Helps Keep Us Safe?

In Nigeria, there is a special group of people who help make sure everyone follows the rules about drugs. They are called the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency. That's a very long name! Let's just call them the "Drug Safety Team." Their job is to find people who are selling or using bad drugs. They want to stop these drugs from hurting people. So, when they found out Esther was selling cannabis, they had to do their job. They had to arrest her because she broke a very important rule, a law, that helps keep everyone safe. It's their job to make sure that these bad plants don't get into the hands of people who might get hurt by them. They are like very important helpers who protect us all.

A Special Country: Nigeria

Our story takes place in Nigeria. Nigeria is a wonderful country in West Africa. It has beautiful beaches, big cities, and lots of different animals. Many people live in Nigeria, and they speak many different languages! It's a place full of life and color. But just like in every country, there are rules that everyone must follow to keep things orderly and safe. And the rule about selling dangerous plants like cannabis is one of the most important ones. Did you know? Africa is the second-biggest continent in the world! Nigeria is one of the biggest countries in Africa!

Why Is This Story So Big?

You might be thinking, "Why is this story so important for me to hear?" Well, it's because of Esther's age! Imagine your great-grandma. She is probably very kind and wise. Most very old people are. So, when someone who is 101 years old is arrested for something like this, it makes everyone think and talk about it. It's unusual because usually, when people break these kinds of rules, they are much younger. It makes people ask questions like, "Why would a very old lady be doing this?" It reminds us that rules are for *everyone*. It doesn't matter how old you are, or how young you are. If a rule helps keep people safe, then everyone should follow it.

What Can We Learn?

So, what can we learn from Esther's story? 1. **Rules are important:** Always listen to grown-ups and follow the rules. Rules help keep you and everyone around you safe and happy. 2. **Drugs can be dangerous:** Remember, some plants and things called drugs are not good for you. Only take medicine from a doctor or a grown-up who knows it's safe. Never take things from strangers. 3. **Stay curious and ask questions:** If you ever see something that doesn't look right, or if you have questions about plants or drugs, always ask a trusted grown-up – your mum, dad, teacher, or older family member. They will help you understand and keep you safe. This story makes us think about why we have laws. It reminds us that even when it's a very old person, the law still needs to protect everyone from things that can cause harm.

Stay Safe and Happy!

We hope Esther's family can help her. It is a sad situation, but it is also a reminder that we all need to follow the rules that keep us safe. Remember to always be kind, be curious, and most importantly, stay safe! I'll be back soon with more news from our amazing continent, Africa! Goodbye for now, my little friends!
summary: A 101-year-old great-grandmother named Esther was arrested in Nigeria because she was selling a plant called cannabis, which is against the rules and not good for people.
whyMatters: This story teaches us that rules are for everyone, even very old people, because some plants can be dangerous, and it's important to always stay safe and listen to grown-ups.
